disease.name: Powdery Mildew
disease.severity_index: Can cause significant yield loss, up to 30–50% if uncontrolled

environmental_factors.temperature_humidity: Prefers cool, humid environments with poor air circulation
environmental_factors.soil_conditions: High nitrogen content in soil can worsen infection

region_specific_information.Andhra Pradesh: Powdery mildew occurs heavily in coastal districts due to high humidity and fog in winter.
region_specific_information.Telangana: The disease is more severe in low-lying areas with poor drainage.

early_stage: Small, white powdery patches on leaves, stems, and pods
Infection starts on lower leaves and spreads upwards
mid_stage: Powdery white fungal growth expands, covering larger leaf areas
Reduced pod formation due to weakened plant health
advanced_stage: Reduced chlorophyll leading to poor photosynthesis
Grain shriveling and low seed quality

proper_irrigation: Improve field aeration by maintaining proper plant spacing
soil_seed_treatment: Treat seeds with Carbendazim 2 g/kg seed to reduce initial infection

cultural_practices: Avoid late sowing to escape peak infection periods
Intercropping with cereals (e.g., sorghum, pearl millet) reduces disease spread
Destroy infected plant debris after harvest to prevent spore carryover
biological_control: Neem Oil @ 5 ml/L water shows some control but is not highly effective
Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/kg seed reduces early fungal attack
